title: Marguerite and the Cipher Revisited
premise: When the coffin of town founder Edmund Vasse is exhumed for a land dispute and found empty, insurance investigator Rafael Hartwell discovers her own late mother's name sewn into the burial shroud — proof her family was entangled with the Vasse fortune decades ago. As Rafael deciphers a cipher hidden in the founder's will, she realizes the killer is someone who has read every archived case file, including hers, and is staging deaths to mirror old unsolved claims. The trail leads to the town's founding families, where love, inheritance, and buried identity collide. In the end Rafael traps the killer — the archivist who raised her — by feeding him a falsified file, and chooses to publish the truth about her parentage rather than protect the town's myth.
about_author: Isandro Blackwood is the pen name of a former records clerk who spent a decade inside municipal archives before turning to fiction. Known for mysteries built on paperwork, memory, and the lies towns tell themselves, Blackwood writes from a coastal New England town much like the one in this novel.

chapters.title: The Exhumation
chapters.summary: Rafael Hartwell attends the court-ordered exhumation of founder Edmund Vasse as the insurer on the mausoleum policy. When the coffin lid lifts, it is empty except for a shroud embroidered with her mother's maiden name. POV: Rafael. Emotional beat: cold professional detachment cracking into personal dread.

chapters.title: Seven Years of Filing
chapters.summary: Rafael walks the reader through her photographic memory of the town's claim files, establishing that she knows every secret ever insured against. The sheriff dismisses the empty coffin as grave robbery. POV: Rafael. Emotional beat: the comfort of order beginning to feel like a cage.

chapters.title: The Shroud's Stitch
chapters.summary: Rafael traces the shroud's embroidery to a defunct seamstress shop once owned by the Vasse estate. She finds a 1960s life-insurance claim bearing her mother's signature as witness. POV: Rafael. Emotional beat: grief resurfacing as obsession.

chapters.title: A Will That Counts Backward
chapters.summary: The probate lawyer reveals Vasse's will contains an odd numeric codicil — a cipher. Rafael recognizes the numbering scheme from old claim forms. Someone else has requested the will's file twice this year. POV: Rafael. Emotional beat: the thrill of the hunt returning.

chapters.title: The Second Empty Grave
chapters.summary: A retired judge from a founding family is found dead; his crypt niche is also empty, staged identically. The killer is repeating a pattern only someone who studied the archives would know. POV: Rafael. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Marguerite
chapters.summary: Rafael finds letters signed 'Marguerite' between Vasse and an unnamed woman — love letters interleaved with financial instructions. Her mother's handwriting matches. POV: Rafael. Emotional beat: identity upended; was her mother the founder's secret?

chapters.title: The Man Who Reads Everything
chapters.summary: Rafael narrows suspects to those with archive access: the town clerk, a rival investigator, and Corwin Ashe, the gentle archivist who helped raise her after her mother died. POV: Rafael. Emotional beat: loyalty at war with suspicion.

chapters.title: Duty's Ledger
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter through archived documents: the Vasse heirs paid out hush-money claims to bury a scandal involving Marguerite. Rafael realizes the 'inheritance' theme runs through every file. POV: alternating Rafael and document excerpts. Emotional beat: the past pressing its palm flat against the present.

chapters.title: An Offer of Silence
chapters.summary: A founding-family descendant offers Rafael money to close the case quietly, revealing they know about her mother. She refuses but pockets a copied page. POV: Rafael. Emotional beat: temptation and pride.

chapters.title: The Cipher Breaks
chapters.summary: Working nights, Rafael cracks the codicil: coordinates pointing beneath the old seamstress shop, and a confession clause — Vasse willed everything to Marguerite's child. POV: Rafael. Emotional beat: vertigo; the child may be her.

chapters.title: What Was Buried Twice
chapters.summary: Beneath the shop, Rafael finds a second coffin — Vasse's actual remains — and evidence he was murdered in 1968, his death disguised as a claim payout. POV: Rafael. Emotional beat: awe curdling into horror.

chapters.title: Corwin's Kindness
chapters.summary: Ashe comforts Rafael over her discoveries, quoting case details he shouldn't know — including the shroud's stitch count, never made public. POV: Rafael. Emotional beat: heartbreak; the father figure becomes the prime suspect.

chapters.title: The Third Staging
chapters.summary: The town clerk is attacked and left alive beside an empty display coffin, a warning. The killer knows Rafael is closing in and wants her to stop — or to finish something. POV: Rafael. Emotional beat: urgency compressing time.

chapters.title: Love Against Duty
chapters.summary: Rafael confronts her feelings for Deputy Sol Reyes, who has been ordered to take her off the case. He chooses to help her off the record. POV: Rafael (with a short Sol interlude). Emotional beat: tenderness as rebellion.

chapters.title: The Archive at Night
chapters.summary: Rafael breaks into the records vault and finds entire decades re-ordered — files rewritten in Ashe's hand, history curated like a shrine. POV: Rafael. Emotional beat: violation; even memory can be forged.

chapters.title: Marguerite's Daughter
chapters.summary: DNA results confirm Rafael is Vasse's great-granddaughter through Marguerite's line — making her the cipher's true heir, and the killer's intended instrument. POV: Rafael. Emotional beat: grief and fury fused into purpose.

chapters.title: The Confession File
chapters.summary: Rafael plants a falsified file claiming she found Vasse's original murder confession naming his killer, and lets word reach the archive. POV: Rafael. Emotional beat: cold clarity; she is now hunting the hunter.

chapters.title: Night in the Mausoleum
chapters.summary: Ashe takes the bait and comes to destroy the file. Rafael confronts him among the tombs; he confesses he killed to complete Marguerite's 'unfinished claim' and restore what he believes is rightfully hers — Rafael's inheritance. POV: Rafael. Emotional beat: climax; love and duty aimed at each other.

chapters.title: Empty Coffins, Full Hands
chapters.summary: Sol arrests Ashe after a near-fatal struggle in the crypt. Ashe's motive reframes everything: he genuinely believed he was serving Rafael's legacy. POV: Rafael. Emotional beat: hollow victory.

chapters.title: Reading the Whole File
chapters.summary: Rafael reads Ashe's curated archive end to end, restoring the tampered records and finding Marguerite's final letter — she chose anonymity over the fortune, for her daughter's sake. POV: Rafael. Emotional beat: understanding without absolution.

chapters.title: The Truth in Print
chapters.summary: Against pressure from the founding families, Rafael publishes the full story, dissolving the town's myth of Vasse and claiming her lineage openly. Sol stands beside her. POV: Rafael. Emotional beat: courage; identity chosen, not inherited.

chapters.title: Marguerite and the Cipher, Closed
chapters.summary: Months later, Rafael reburies Vasse's remains properly and files one last claim — closing her mother's seven-year-old open case. The archive is finally alphabetized, and she is finally free of it. POV: Rafael. Emotional beat: quiet resolution; the file closes, the woman doesn't.
